17:23 Local Time, 13:23 GMT, 18:53 IST: One wicket in the first half of the day and five in the second. Given how things have unfolded over the last three days, that's a significant uptick. Resuming on 97, skipper Rahmat Shah showed tremendous grit and determination, adding a valuable 92 runs with Zia-ur-Rehman for the 8th wicket before eventually falling for a magnificent 173 off 347 balls. The pair batted for 40 overs, and it took a third new ball to finally break their resistance. From Zimbabwe's perspective, Newman Nyamhuri deserved a five-wicket haul for his relentless efforts on a lifeless surface, and he eventually got there by claiming the final Afghanistan wicket.

Zimbabwe lost Kaia and Curran cheaply, but Taylor and Bennett once again displayed great composure to steady the innings. While Taylor batted with fluency, Bennett blended caution with positive intent to put together an 82-run stand for the third wicket. Just when things seemed to be falling into place, an unfortunate run-out brought Taylor's innings to an end. Things could have been even better for Afghanistan had Rahmat held on to a catch offered by Ervine on nought, but it wasn't to be. Zimbabwe now have a lead of 154 and will look to bat for at least another session and a half before entertaining thoughts of a declaration. A collapse or an adventurous declaration looks highly unlikely, and unless something dramatic happens, this contest seems to be heading towards a rather predictable draw.
